Manchester City.raw_text:
Jeremy Doku (calf), who came off at half-time in the Community Shield, is City’s only absentee this weekend.
Matheus Nunes suffered an injury in the warm-up at Wembley and had to withdraw from the squad but is fine.
TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR
Xavi Simons (knee), Wilson Odobert (knee) and Dejan Kulusevski (knee) are still out, although fellow long-term absentee Mohammed Kudus (thigh) is “close”.
There’s mixed news on Pedro Porro , Destiniy Udogie , Micky van de Ven and Dominic Solanke , meanwhile.
The first three haven’t played for the Lilywhites this summer. While Porro’s no-shows are down to a deep run in the World Cup, van de Ven and Udogie have been nursing minor issues. Solanke, meanwhile, has not featured since a 45-minute run-out against Chelsea on August 1.
Two are fit and two are not, while James Maddison and Matheus Fernandes , who featured in what was effectively a B-team friendly last weekend, will be involved this weekend.
Pape Matar Sarr (abductor) is another addition to the injury list.
BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION
Carlos Baleba (ankle) and Yankuba Minteh (leg) remain on the sidelines, all while the transfer rumour mill heavily links them to other clubs. Minteh is out for 2-3 months out but Baleba shouldn’t be too far away.
Evan Ferguson (ankle), Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring) and Stefanos Tzimas (knee) are still out, too.
There were some reports that Diego Gomez limped down the tunnel after his withdrawal last Saturday but he recovered from whatever that was and lasted 68 minutes in Thursday’s draw with Tromso.
Promise David has had his first training session with his new teammates and could be in the squad on Sunday.

Everton.raw_text:
Everton will be without three central midfielders for their Gameweek 1 clash with Crystal Palace.
James Garner underwent successful surgery to address a groin issue in July, while new boy Christian Norgaard has gone under the knife for the same reason.
Tim Iroegbunam , heavily linked with a move to Hull City, is out with a groin problem of his own.

Brentford.raw_text:
Keith Andrews has confirmed that Sepp van den Berg will miss the first few weeks of the season.
The defender has a groin abductor issue which has affected his pre-season.

Tom Cairney (knee) will be out until after the September international break but he is the only injury-related absentee.

Chelsea.raw_text:
Xabi Alonso actually faced the media on Thursday night, with quotes embargoed until this afternoon.
Speaking then, Alonso said he was hopeful Moises Caicedo (unspecified) would be ready to face Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday.
Alonso hinted earlier this week that Marco Palestra (unspecified) wouldn’t recover in time for Gameweek 2. Jordan Henderson (wrist) is also still sidelined.
Levi Colwill and Geovany Quenda , who didn’t feature in Thursday’s cup win over Luton Town, are fine, however.
Alonso hinted that Reece James and Cole Palmer would start again, despite surprisingly doing so on Thursday.
Meanwhile, Wesley Fofana returns from a ban.
Alonso said he “knows” who will start in goal on Sunday – but wouldn’t say who that will be.

Manchester United.raw_text:
Amad Diallo (unspecified) and Carlos Baleba (ankle) will miss the Ipswich game this weekend. Both are hoping to return before the international break.
Mason Mount (knock) is back in training.
Manuel Ugarte (knee) is out long term, while we await to hear whether Matthijs de Ligt (back) is ready for a playing comeback despite a return to training
BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION
Georginio Rutter could return after missing the midweek UEFA Conference League tie with Tromso with a minor problem.
But there’s a fresh injury blow concerning Jack Hinshelwood , who also sat out Thursday’s win.
Fabian Hurzeler says Hinshelwood’s issue is not a big one but his involvement in Gameweek 2 looks very doubtful, and there are even reports from external sources suggesting a 5-6 week absence.
Yankuba Minteh (leg), Evan Ferguson (ankle), Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring) and Stefanos Tzimas (knee) are all out, too.
New signings Promise David and Jaouen Hadjam should be involved, however.
TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR
Mohammed Kudus (thigh) could make his long-awaited return from injury as a substitute this weekend.
Omar Marmoush and Savio are also poised for their debuts, although Roberto De Zerbi says decisions over whether to start them – as well as Pedro Porro, who was late back from World Cup duty, and Micky van de Ven, who had a disrupted pre-season – or not are still to be made.
Xavi Simons (knee), Wilson Odobert (knee) and Dejan Kulusevski (knee) are still sidelined.
James Maddison (shoulder) is also a concern.
Pape Matar Sarr (abductor) is “good” but looks set for a move away.

Liam Delap has joined Forest this week and could make his debut.

Ollie Watkins is Saudi-bound, while Tammy Abraham – who limped out of Aston Villa’s final pre-season friendly and hasn’t featured since – is apparently off to Ipswich Town.
Nicolas Jackson is on his way in, however, and Unai Emery is hopeful he’ll be registered in time to face the Gunners.

Everton.raw_text:
David Moyes says Hayden Hackney is “touch and go” ahead of Everton’s clash with Bournemouth this weekend.
Hackney missed the midweek Carabao Cup clash at Preston with an ankle issue.
Christian Nørgaard (groin) remains sidelined for now.
Meanwhile, Moyes says the fit-again James Garner needs more game-time after missing the majority of pre-season with a hernia injury.
Away from injuries, Moyes was asked whether there was any truth in the rumours suggesting Iliman Ndiaye and Jack Grealish could be heading in opposite directions.
